thought.text: The page is a Vue SPA — CSRF token is in the meta tag. Let me retry the login POST using it.

reasoning_content: The sign-in page is a Vue SPA — there's no server-rendered form, and the CSRF token is in a meta tag. The Vue app POSTs via axios. Let me use the meta tag's CSRF token to try the login API. Devise usually accepts the authenticity_token in the POST body. Let me try with the meta token.

action.command:
cd /tmp
rm -f cj.txt
curl -sS -c cj.txt -o signin.html http://localhost:3000/users/sign-in
TOKEN=$(grep -oE 'csrf-token" content="[^"]*"' signin.html | sed 's/.*content="//;s/"//')
echo "token len: ${#TOKEN}"
TOKEN_ENC=$(printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | sed 's/[+\/]/&/g')
# URL-encode properly using ruby
TENC=$(ruby -ruri -e 'print URI.encode(ARGV[0])' "$TOKEN")
curl -sS -b cj.txt -c cj.txt -L -o login.html -w "FINAL_URL=%{url_effective} HTTP_CODE=%{http_code}\n" \
  -X POST http://localhost:3000/users/sign-in \
  --data-urlencode "authenticity_token=$TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "user[email]=admin@example.org" \
  --data-urlencode "user[password]=TTOF3UHA0bsQ"
grep -o "<title>[^<]*</title>" login.html 2>/dev/null || head -3 login.html
